## IGNITE CAPSTONE

## Bringing in the Data and Setting up the Library

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(ggpubr)

IGNITE_Data_Sheet <- read_excel("IGNITE Data Sheet.xlsx", 
                                sheet = "RCoding")

```

Data is already really clean, will save the chunk below in case of data cleaning

```{r}
#data cleaning here!
#There is one reading of black mustard that is 600 FMC, will take that out

IGNITE_Data_Sheet_2 <- IGNITE_Data_Sheet |> 
  filter( FMC < 500) |> 
  mutate(Site = as.factor(Site))


```

Exploratory Data Graphing

```{r}
ggplot(IGNITE_Data_Sheet_2) +
  aes(x = Species, y = FMC, fill = as.factor(Site)) + 
  geom_col()+
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2")+
  theme_bw()


ggplot(IGNITE_Data_Sheet_2)+
  aes(x = Species, y = Wet_Mass)+
  geom_boxplot()+
  theme_bw()

ggplot(IGNITE_Data_Sheet_2)+
  aes(x = Species, y = Dry_Mass)+
  geom_boxplot()+
  theme_bw()
```

In this very rough estimate you can see that our buckwheat had the highest combined FMC for the first sampling event

We need to collect alot more of each species, 2 inches from four sides of the plant (8 inches total) is not enough (except for lemonade berry

Sagebrush dried the most between wet and dry weight

```{r}

IGNITE_Summary <- IGNITE_Data_Sheet_2 |> 
  group_by(Species, Site ) |> 
  summarize(Mean_FMC = mean(FMC, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_FMC = sd(FMC, na.rm = TRUE))

ggplot(IGNITE_Summary) +
  aes(x = Species, y = Mean_FMC, fill = Species)+
  geom_col(position = "dodge")+
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Mean_FMC - sd_FMC, 
                ymax = Mean_FMC + sd_FMC, width = 0.5))+
                  facet_wrap(Site~.)+
                  theme_bw()

```

The sagebrush error bars in site 4 can be explained by the very different masses collected at the site

```{r}
ggplot(IGNITE_Summary) +
  aes(x = Species, y = Mean_FMC, fill = Species)+
  geom_col(position = "dodge")+
  theme_bw()


```

Mustard's numbers are inflated due to having little to 0 wet mass

## Statistics

Tests for Normality

```{r}
ggplot(IGNITE_Data_Sheet_2)+
  aes(x = FMC)+
  geom_histogram()
#Data does not look that normal, will proceed

FMC_model <- lmer(FMC~Species + Phenology + Percent_Green + (1 | Site/Bottle_ID), data = IGNITE_Data_Sheet_2)

plot(FMC_model, which = "2")

ggqqplot(residuals(FMC_model))

summary(FMC_model)
anova(FMC_model, type = "2")
```

There are significant differences between species and phenology (need to look more into this one )
